title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
competency: Identify that forces act between objects and can be measured. Describe everyday situations that demonstrate balanced and unbalanced forces.
objectives: Define force and identify its unit of measurement.
Differentiate between balanced and unbalanced forces.
Explain how unbalanced forces cause changes in the motion of an object.
Identify the net force acting on an object in various scenarios.
introduction: Why does a ball start rolling when you kick it? Why does a heavy box stay still even when you push it lightly? Everything that moves (or stays still) is affected by 'Forces.' In this lesson, we will explore the tug-of-war between forces and how they determine the movement of everything around us.
content:
1. What is Force?

A Force is simply a push or a pull acting upon an object as a result of its interaction with another object. Forces have two main characteristics:

  • Magnitude: The 'strength' or size of the force.
  • Direction: Where the force is pointing (North, South, Left, Right, etc.).

The standard unit of force is the Newton (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton. It is measured using a tool called a Spring Balance.

2. Balanced Forces

When the forces acting on an object are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, they are Balanced. In this state:

  • The Net Force is zero (0 N).
  • There is NO change in motion.
  • If the object is at rest, it stays at rest. If it is moving, it continues moving at a constant speed in a straight line.

3. Unbalanced Forces

When the forces acting on an object are not equal, they are Unbalanced. In this state:

  • The Net Force is greater than zero.
  • The object will accelerate (change its speed or direction).
  • The object always moves in the direction of the stronger force.

4. Calculating Net Force

To find the Net Force:

  • If forces are in the same direction, ADD them.
  • If forces are in opposite directions, SUBTRACT the smaller force from the larger one.

examples.title: A Book on a Table
examples.description: Gravity pulls the book down with 5N, while the table pushes up with 5N. The forces are balanced (Net Force = 0N), so the book remains still.

examples.title: Tug-of-War
examples.description: Team A pulls with 100N to the left. Team B pulls with 120N to the right. The forces are unbalanced. The Net Force is 20N to the right, so Team B wins!

keyTerms.definition: The total or combination of all forces acting on an object.
The SI unit used to measure the magnitude of a force.
A change in an object's speed or direction caused by an unbalanced force.

keyConcepts: Forces always come in pairs and act in specific directions.
Balanced forces do not cause a change in motion.
An unbalanced force is required to start, stop, or change the direction of an object.
summary: Force is a push or pull measured in Newtons. When forces are balanced, the object’s motion remains unchanged because the net force is zero. However, when forces are unbalanced, the net force causes the object to speed up, slow down, or change direction.

selfCheck.q: What is the standard unit of force?
If two people push a car in the same direction with 50N each, what is the net force?
True or False: An object moving at a constant speed in a straight line has balanced forces acting on it.
selfCheck.a: True (There is no change in motion, so net force is 0N).
